source_text: Sive per visum sive per tactum sive per auditum sive per odoratum sive per gus tum. Tolle denique malignae huius stirpis radicem et statim te ipsam spiritalem contemplaris. " Radix enim - ait Scriptura - omnium malorum concupiscentia " [n213] . Vides, quo spiritu et propter quod dogma Manichaeus concupiscentiam carnis incessat hanc dicens legem esse peccati, quae si a corporibus auferretur, spiritalem se filia eius, ad quam scribit, factam videret. Quam opinionem quibus Apostoli nitatur confirmare sententiis audiamus: " Caro enim adversatur spiritui ", quia filia concupiscentiae est, " et spiritus carni " [n214] , quia filius animae est.
pass_a_gloss: Whether through sight or through touch or through hearing or through smell or through taste. Take away finally the root of this malign stock and immediately you contemplate yourself spiritual. For the root, says Scripture, of all evils is desire. You see by what spirit and on account of what dogma the Manichaean attacks the desire of the flesh, saying this is the law of sin, which if it were taken away from bodies, his daughter, to whom he writes, would see herself made spiritual. By which sentences of the Apostle he strives to confirm which opinion let us hear: For flesh is adverse to spirit, because it is the daughter of desire, and spirit to flesh, because it is the son of the soul.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: ‘Whether through sight, touch, hearing, smell, or taste. Remove, then, the root of this evil stock, and immediately you see yourself as spiritual. For Scripture says: “Desire is the root of all evils” (Romans 7:23)’ (compare 1 Timothy 6:10).

You see in what spirit and for what doctrine Mani attacks fleshly desire, calling it the law of sin: if it were removed from bodies, his daughter, to whom he writes, would see that she had become spiritual. Let us hear which statements of the apostle he tries to use to establish this opinion: ‘“The flesh opposes the spirit,” because it is the daughter of desire; “and the spirit the flesh,” because it is the son of the soul’ (Galatians 5:17).

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
